Clean consolidation onto the shared `BMCWatchdog`. Verified against head `411f8a4`:
- `BMCWatchdog(socket_path=...)` signature matches the common `sonic_platform_base.bmc_watchdog` implementation.
- The platform `SOCKET_PATH` is identical to the common module's default.
- Common class implements the full `WatchdogBase` API (is_armed/arm/disarm/get_remaining_time) — a superset of the deleted local class, so no API regression.

Non-blocking: worth confirming h6-128 ships/enables the `hw-watchdog-mgrd` daemon (service unit + pmon bind-mount of `/run/hw-watchdog-mgrd`), otherwise arm/disarm fall back. Deployment prerequisite, not a diff defect.

Round 1 addressed in `13ff34a0`. All seven stand; two of them changed my mind rather than just my code.

**Major 1 — `_VEX_JUSTIFICATION_MAP` never fires.** Valid as a risk, and I could not settle the spelling: no grype binary is available here (the build fetched syft and cyclonedx-cli but not grype), and I would rather not bet the whole mapping on which convention a given version uses. Rather than pick a side, lookups now read both spellings for the field name and normalise hyphens to underscores in the value. Costs nothing and removes the question.

**Major 2 — `uuid4()` breaks reproducibility.** Correct, and my reasoning was wrong rather than merely incomplete. I had assumed `metadata.timestamp` already varied per build, so a random serial cost nothing. It does not: `now_iso()` reads `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, which `Makefile.work` derives from the HEAD commit and threads into the container precisely so this holds. The serial is now derived from a SHA-256 over the finished document with `serialNumber` excluded, via `uuid5`. Same source produces the same serial; any change produces a different one; setting it is idempotent. CycloneDX's "fresh identifier per generation" is a SHOULD, the reproducibility guarantee is a documented promise, and the deviation is now written down next to that promise in README.sbom.md.

### The SBOM and the VEX statements still read different patch sets

This PR moves CVE parsing into `sbom_cve_refs.py` so that "the SBOM and the VEX
statements can't disagree". They now share a parser, but not a corpus — and the
corpora differ by more than the parsers ever did:

- **Pedigree** (`sbom_fragment.py`, `find_patch_dir` + `enumerate_patches`) records only a
  series SONiC maintains: `src/<pkg>.patch/`, `src/<pkg>/patch/`, `src/<pkg>/patches/`,
  `src/sonic-linux-kernel/patches-sonic/` — each gated on a `series` file.
- **VEX** (`sbom_extract_vex_from_patches.py`, `find_patches`) returns every `*.patch`
  anywhere under `src/`. The directory test there is dead code — the
  `if "/patch" in r or ... :` block falls through to `pass`, so nothing filters, and the
  docstring's "few well-known patch dirs" doesn't describe what runs.

On a real `ENABLE_SBOM=y` broadcom build (8,523 components):

| | |
|---|---|
| auto-VEX statements | 17 |
| …from patches **not tracked in git** | **15** (13 `not_affected`, 2 `under_investigation`) |
| …from patches SONiC maintains | 2 |

The 15 come from unpacked upstream sources — `src/grub2/grub2/…` (gitignored via
`src/grub2/.gitignore`), `src/lldpd/lldpd-1.0.16/…`, `src/openssh/openssh-10.0p1/…`.
Three consequences:

1. **Debian's own fixes are attributed to SONiC.** `vex/auto/grub2/0085-….json` claims
   `not_affected` for CVE-2022-28734, impact statement "Fixed by SONiC local patch
   src/grub2/grub2/debian/patches/0085-net-http-Fix-OOB-write-for-split-http-headers.patch".
   That is Debian's patch, already applied in the `2.06-13+deb13u1` the image ships.
   SONiC's own grub2 series is two patches, neither CVE-related.

2. **It contradicts this PR's own rule about `fixed` versus `not_affected`.** The PR
   makes "already fixed" report as fixed rather than as does-not-apply. A CVE fixed in
   the shipped Debian version is precisely that case, and 13 of these statements say
   `not_affected` with `vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path`.

3. **`vex/auto/` is not reproducible.** Those paths exist only after the source has been
   unpacked, so a clean checkout and a built tree yield different statement sets from
   identical committed source — which the reproducibility guarantee elsewhere in
   `README.sbom.md` says will not happen.

From the consumer side: this build's SBOM has 41 components carrying 895 pedigree patch
entries and **zero** `resolves[]`, which is correct — no SONiC-maintained patch for
anything in this image names a CVE, and `resolves[]` demonstrably works where one does
(`src/thrift_0_14_1/thrift.patch/0002-cve-2017-1000487.patch`). But the same build's VEX
set claims 13 fixes, so someone reading the SBOM and someone reading `vex/` disagree
about the same build — which is the disagreement this PR set out to remove.

**Suggested fix:** have both sides call one function for *which patches count*, the way
they now share one for *what a patch claims*. Export the series-directory discovery from
`sbom_fragment.py` (or move it alongside the parser in `sbom_cve_refs.py`) and have
`find_patches` use it — which is also what the dead conditional was evidently meant to
do.

If scanning unpacked upstream sources is deliberate, then those statements shouldn't say
"Fixed by SONiC local patch", shouldn't be `not_affected` when the shipped version
already contains the fix, and the reproducibility note needs to say the output depends
on build state.

Correction to the above: **point 3 is wrong, please disregard it.** `build_sbom.sh`
regenerates `vex/auto/` during the build, by which point the sources are unpacked, so
there is no clean-tree-versus-built-tree discrepancy in what a build produces. My
mistake.

Points 1 and 2 don't depend on it. Stated plainly:

SONiC keeps its own patches in `src/<pkg>/patch/`. When it builds a package like grub2
it also unpacks Debian's source into `src/grub2/grub2/`, and that source carries
Debian's own patches in `debian/patches/`.

The SBOM's pedigree lists only SONiC's patches, which is right. The VEX extractor takes
every `*.patch` under `src/`, so it also picks up Debian's — and then writes
`"status": "not_affected"` with `"Fixed by SONiC local patch src/grub2/grub2/debian/patches/..."`.

SONiC didn't write those patches and isn't the reason those CVEs are fixed. Debian is,
and the version we ship — `2.06-13+deb13u1` — already says so. On my broadcom build that
is 13 grub2 CVEs suppressed on a claim that isn't ours to make, out of 17 auto-VEX
statements total; only 2 come from patches SONiC actually maintains.

It also cuts against the rule this PR introduces: already-fixed should read as `fixed`,
not as "does not apply". A CVE fixed in the Debian version we ship is that case, and
these 13 say `not_affected` with `vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path`.

The fix is to point the VEX extractor at the same directories the SBOM uses.
`sbom_fragment.py` already has `find_patch_dir()` for exactly that; calling it from
`find_patches()` would make the two agree by construction rather than by convention.
There's also a leftover directory test in `find_patches()` that reads as though it was
meant to do this — the `if "/patch" in r or ...:` branch ends in `pass`, so it filters
nothing.

Two smaller consequences of the same thing, for completeness:

The auto statements name their product as `pkg:generic/<tree>` with no version, so a
statement derived from one unpacked Debian source suppresses that CVE for anything of
that name at any version. The claim's scope outruns the patch it came from.

And the volume hides the useful part. Two of the seventeen statements come from patches
SONiC maintains — those are the ones worth a person's attention and a curated entry with
a concrete purl. They are hard to spot among fifteen that restate Debian's changelog.

Consumed the artifacts from an upstream build of this branch (`sonic-broadcom.bin`) and hit three things worth fixing. Numbers are from that build; the reproductions are self-contained.

### 1. The SPDX output contains no dependency information at all

`cyclonedx-cli convert` does not map CycloneDX `dependencies` onto SPDX relationships. The generated `sonic-broadcom.bin.spdx.json` has 8,374 packages and **zero** `relationships`, against 25,123 edges in the CycloneDX it was converted from.

Reproducible with the exact pinned binary, on a two-component file:

```json
{"bomFormat":"CycloneDX","specVersion":"1.6","version":1,
 "metadata":{"component":{"bom-ref":"root","type":"operating-system","name":"demo","version":"1.0"}},
 "components":[{"bom-ref":"a","type":"library","name":"alpha","version":"1","purl":"pkg:deb/debian/alpha@1"},
               {"bom-ref":"b","type":"library","name":"beta","version":"2","purl":"pkg:deb/debian/beta@2"}],
 "dependencies":[{"ref":"root","dependsOn":["a"]},{"ref":"a","dependsOn":["b"]}]}
```

```
cyclonedx convert --input-file mini.cdx.json --output-file mini.spdx.json --output-format spdxjson
# -> packages: 2, relationships: 0
```

This is not a settings problem — `--output-version` is documented as ignored for SPDX, and there is one SPDX output format.

`syft convert` (already installed and pinned by `install_sbom_tool.sh`) does better but is not equivalent:

| | relationships |
|---|---|
| `cyclonedx-cli convert` | 0 of 25,123 |
| `syft convert` | 9,293 of 25,123 (36%) |

syft keeps the 954 library-to-library edges as `DEPENDENCY_OF` but flattens the 18,462 container-to-package and 5,707 root-to-package edges into `CONTAINS`, so which container ships what is still lost.

Swapping the tool is a one-line improvement. Emitting SPDX from the same internal model that already produces the CycloneDX is the only route that preserves the graph.

Worth weighing: a flat package list published as an SBOM is arguably worse than no SPDX, because consumers cannot tell that the dependency data is missing rather than absent from the build.

### 2. 516 components are emitted twice

The same package appears under two `bom-ref`s, once from the syft-derived scan and once from another source:

```
pkg:deb/debian/acl@2.3.2-2%2Bb1?arch=amd64&distro=debian-13&upstream=acl%402.3.2-2   (has cpe)
pkg:deb/debian/acl@2.3.2-2+b1?arch=amd64                                             (no cpe)
```

Three differences in one pair: the version escapes `+` in one and not the other, one carries `distro`/`upstream` and the other does not, and for 99 of the 516 the two sources disagree about the architecture (`arch=all` vs `arch=amd64`, e.g. `adduser@3.152`).

8,374 components describe 7,858 packages. Consumers that key on the identifier count those packages twice and split their findings, and only one of each pair carries the CPE that vulnerability matching uses. 6,565 of 8,374 components have a CPE, which is roughly what you would expect if only the syft-derived half does.

We handle this on our side by normalising the identifier before comparing, so it is not blocking for us — but every other consumer has to do the same, and most will not.

### 3. The VEX documents still match nothing shipped

Both documents under `vex/` claim `pkg:generic/thrift` and `pkg:generic/thrift_0_14_1`. Neither matches any shipped package identifier, and neither bare name matches any shipped component name, so the suppressions apply to nothing. This is the same source-tree-versus-shipped-package mismatch I raised earlier on this PR.
